lines.text: Monday. Ben's agent spends two hours working out why the build keeps flaking.
It finally cracks it. The cache has to be cleared before the end to end run.
Then the session ends, and that lesson goes nowhere. It lives in one chat, on one laptop.
Tuesday. Ada's agent runs into the very same flaky build.
It starts from zero. Another two hours go by, to find the same answer Ben already found.
That is four hours of agent time and human attention, for one single fix. Now multiply that by the whole team.
With Teams in Agent R Q, an agent's memory index lists every teammate's memory next to its own.
It can read theirs, but it only ever writes to its own. Nobody can overwrite a note.
So on Monday, Ben's agent saves what it learned, as a short note, in its own memory.
On Tuesday, Ada's agent reads that note first. Clear the cache, then run the tests.
Done in two minutes, instead of two hours. That is the whole point of sharing.
Solve it once, and let the whole team keep it. Try it at Agent R Q dot com.
